title: LinkedIn MCP Server: What Exists and What’s Safe (2026)
summary: LinkedIn has no public MCP server, only two apps in ChatGPT. Every LinkedIn MCP option compared, what LinkedIn’s terms allow, and the safe route per job.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- **LinkedIn has no public MCP server.** There is no endpoint to add to Claude, Cursor or any other client.
- LinkedIn does ship **two apps inside ChatGPT** : "LinkedIn" (look up a professional) and "LinkedIn Ads" (read-only ad set performance, in beta).
- Everything else is third party, in two kinds: tools on LinkedIn’s **official APIs** (posting, company pages, ads) and **scrapers** that drive your logged-in session (profiles, messages, people search).
- LinkedIn’s User Agreement forbids the second kind, and accounts using them get restricted.


Current as of September 21, 2026.


"LinkedIn MCP" is eight different requests wearing one name. Posting as yourself has a sanctioned route. Reading other people’s profiles does not. Which one you mean decides both the tool and the risk, so this guide takes them one at a time. If ads are the job, go straight to[LinkedIn Ads over MCP](https://www.sprites.ai/mcp/linkedin-ads) .


"Limited" means an official API exists but only approved partners can use it. "Against terms" means the only routes that exist automate your account.


## Does LinkedIn have an official MCP server?


No public one. LinkedIn’s developer documentation covers OAuth, Marketing, Sales, Talent and Compliance APIs and no MCP server, and Claude’s connector directory has no LinkedIn connector.


What LinkedIn has built lives inside ChatGPT. ChatGPT apps run on MCP under the hood, which is why the distinction matters:


- [LinkedIn](https://chatgpt.com/apps/linkedin/asdk_app_69949aa62bf48191be5e57a01202beca) looks up a professional and links to their profile. It is a lookup, not a data export.
- [LinkedIn Ads](https://chatgpt.com/apps/linkedin-ads/asdk_app_69cdf9990c90819185974d8727ef9d73) is a read-only beta for ad set performance. It cannot create, pause or change anything.


Both work in ChatGPT and nowhere else. If you use Claude, Cursor, Copilot or your own agent, there is no LinkedIn-published server to connect to, and everything below is a third party.


## What LinkedIn’s rules actually say


Worth reading before choosing a server, because several of the first results break them. LinkedIn’s[User Agreement](https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement) , section 8.2, lists what members agree not to do, including:


- using software, scripts or bots "to scrape or copy the Services, including profiles";
- using another person’s account, "such as sharing log-in credentials or copying cookies";
- using "bots or other unauthorized automated methods" to send messages or create, like and share posts.


The[help centre](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a1341387) spells out the consequence: people who use scraping or automation software "risk having their accounts restricted or shut down", and the tools can become non-operational without notice. LinkedIn’s[automated activity page](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a1340567) describes the restriction and how an account is re-enabled. LinkedIn also enforces this in court: hiQ Labs ended its scraping case in December 2022 under a permanent injunction, and Proxycurl shut down in July 2025 after LinkedIn sued it that January.


The line is simple. **A tool that uses LinkedIn’s official APIs through its own approved app is fine. A tool that drives your logged-in session, or needs your cookie, is automating your account.**


## The official routes an MCP server can use


API What it allows Who can use it


[Sign In with LinkedIn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/authentication/getting-access) Your own name, headline, photo and email Any developer


[Share on LinkedIn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/authentication/getting-access) Post, comment and like as the signed-in member Any developer


[Community Management API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/community-management-app-review) Company page posts, comments and analytics Registered organizations with a commercial use case, after review


[Advertising API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/increasing-access) Campaigns, audiences, lead forms and reporting Approved apps; edits on up to five ad accounts until the Standard tier


Sales Navigator Sales Navigator data inside partner tools Sales Navigator partners only


Talent APIs Job posting, apply flows, recruiter sync Talent partners only


What is missing is the point. **No open permission reads other members’ profiles, searches people or sends messages.** Any server offering those is either a LinkedIn partner, which none of the popular ones are, or automating your account.

The most popular community server,` stickerdaniel/linkedin-mcp-server` , is also the most capable, and honest about it. It drives a real browser logged in as you, can import your session from Chrome, Brave or Edge, and exposes profile lookups, people search, your inbox and sending messages. Its README says LinkedIn prohibits automated access and that accounts using such tools "can be restricted or banned". Take it at its word.


Older servers that promise people search over the official API, such as` felipfr/linkedin-mcpserver` , call endpoints the open permissions do not grant, and have had no commits since March 2025. Expect them to fail.


## Which one to use, by what you are doing


- **Writing and scheduling your own posts:** Taplio or ContentIn. Both publish without scraping or browser automation, and both learn your voice.
- **One-off posting from an automation:** Zapier or Composio. Cheap and sanctioned, and blind to what performs.
- **Company page content:** a tool on the Community Management API, or Zapier’s company update action.
- **Prospecting and people research:** Sales Navigator, in the browser, by a person. There is no sanctioned MCP route, and the account at risk is yours.
- **LinkedIn Ads:**[Sprites](https://www.sprites.ai/mcp/linkedin-ads) to run campaigns with approval, or LinkedIn’s own ChatGPT app for read-only numbers.


## LinkedIn in Claude and ChatGPT, through Sprites


[Sprites](https://www.sprites.ai/) is an AI marketing agent with its own MCP server, and LinkedIn Ads is one of its channels, connected through LinkedIn’s official Advertising API. From Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client, it:


- reads campaign groups, campaigns, ads, lead forms and audiences, and answers performance questions about them;

It does not read people’s profiles, search members or touch your inbox, because there is no sanctioned route to do so. ## LinkedIn MCP questions


### Does LinkedIn have an official MCP server?


Not one you can connect to. LinkedIn publishes no MCP endpoint for Claude, Cursor or any other client. It does ship two first-party apps inside ChatGPT — "LinkedIn", which looks up a professional, and "LinkedIn Ads", a read-only beta for ad set performance — and those work in ChatGPT only.


### Is there a Claude MCP for LinkedIn?


Not from LinkedIn. Claude’s connector directory has no LinkedIn connector. LinkedIn reaches Claude through third parties: for ads, Sprites, Supermetrics or Windsor.ai; for posting, Taplio or ContentIn, added as custom connectors.


### What is the URL for the LinkedIn MCP server?


There is no official one. Every LinkedIn MCP URL belongs to a third party — for example mcp.taplio.com for posting through Taplio, or mcp.sprites.ai/mcp for LinkedIn Ads through Sprites — and each one only reaches what its own LinkedIn integration is allowed to.


### How do I get Claude to scrape LinkedIn?


You can, with a session-based server or a scraping API, and LinkedIn’s User Agreement forbids it: it bans software that scrapes profiles and the copying of cookies, and LinkedIn restricts accounts that use such tools. Use Sales Navigator in the browser for prospecting, and an official-API tool for anything automated.


### Can ChatGPT scrape LinkedIn profiles?


No. LinkedIn’s own app in ChatGPT looks up a professional and links to their profile; it does not export profile data. Bulk profile data only comes from third-party scrapers, which LinkedIn’s User Agreement prohibits.


### Will I get banned for using a LinkedIn MCP server?


You can be restricted for using one that automates your account. LinkedIn’s help centre says users of scraping or automation software "risk having their accounts restricted or shut down". Servers built on LinkedIn’s official APIs — posting, company pages, ads — carry no such risk.


### Can an MCP server post to LinkedIn for me?


Yes, legitimately. LinkedIn’s open "Share on LinkedIn" permission lets an app post, comment and like on your behalf, and company pages go through the Community Management API. Taplio, ContentIn, Zapier and Composio post through LinkedIn’s own APIs rather than your browser.


### Is there a LinkedIn Ads MCP server?


Not a public one from LinkedIn — only the read-only LinkedIn Ads app inside ChatGPT. Hosted options such as Sprites read and change LinkedIn campaigns through the Advertising API, with each change held for approval. The full comparison is on the LinkedIn Ads MCP page.
